summary: Responds to RFC 110 with new rules for using IBM 2741 terminals on the network. The author argues the earlier conventions were inconsistent and hard to use, and that some 2741 keyboards lack characters such as less-than, greater-than and vertical bar. The proposed conventions avoid them.

eli5.summary: Some typewriter keyboards are missing keys, so the earlier plan did not work for everyone. This note suggests a new plan that never needs the missing keys.

questions: how to avoid missing characters on a 2741 terminal
which keys does the correspondence 2741 lack
subtitle: Revised keying conventions so an IBM 2741 terminal can reach network hosts without the keys it lacks.

tldr.problem: The conventions in RFC 110 for using an IBM 2741 as a console were inconsistent and hard to use, and they relied on characters that the correspondence 2741 keyboard does not have.
tldr.mechanism: Only two functions get a single key, character escape (the cent sign) and character delete (backspace). All other special functions are two-key combinations that start with the escape.
tldr.outcome: The proposal replaces the conventions of RFC 110 and avoids the characters less than, greater than, logical not and vertical bar.

facts.label: Missing 2741 characters
facts.value: less than, greater than, logical not, vertical bar

today: RFC 135 updates RFC 110, and the unit metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes it. It is a 1971 proposal for one terminal type on the early network.

sections.title: Why Replace RFC 110
sections.content:
The author proposes conventions to replace those of RFC 110, which he finds inconsistent and difficult to use. The 2741 terminal with a correspondence keyboard lacks several standard characters: less than, greater than, logical not and vertical bar. No convention that wants to support it can use them.

Dedicating a key to a special function is a trade-off. It is convenient as a single key, but entering that character as data then takes two keys. The author concludes that only two functions deserve a dedicated key.
sections.eli5: If a keyboard has no star key, a game that needs the star key cannot be played on it. So the rules should only use keys everyone has.

sections.title: The Special Functions
sections.content:
The character escape is the cent sign, which is on both the regular and correspondence 2741 and is not in the ASCII character set. The character delete is the backspace key. Every other function is the escape followed by a defining key.

Two functions are new. Line continuation lets one logical line be entered on several physical lines when it is longer than the carriage or margin allows. ASCII control is the escape followed by @ and then a standard two or three character abbreviation, which enters any ASCII control character, such as ESC or LF. The escape followed by a plain letter already acts like holding control and that letter.
sections.eli5: One special key says the next key means something special. Every shortcut is that key plus one more.

sections.title: Entering Missing Characters
sections.content:
Eight ASCII graphics appear on neither 2741 keyboard, and the cent sign and backspace must also be enterable as plain data. The proposal gives each a two-key form that begins with the escape. For example, the escape followed by ( stands for [, followed by ) stands for ], followed by 6 stands for { and followed by 9 stands for }.

Escape followed by escape gives the cent sign itself, and escape followed by backspace gives a real backspace. The RFC repeats that < and > are not on the correspondence 2741 and should not be used.
sections.eli5: If a letter is missing from your keyboard, you press the special key and then a stand-in key, like writing a secret code for the missing letter.
